rfm_tuples.R: 'On February 12, 2024, Opco and the parties to the Credit Agreement entered into Amendment No. 2 to the Credit Agreement, which (a) modifies the financial performance covenant ... by temporarily increasing the 4.50:1.00 maximum consolidated first lien net leverage ratio permitted by the covenant to (i) 6.00:1.00 (for the second and third quarters of 2024), (ii) 5.50:1.00 (for the fourth quarter of 2024), (iii) 5.25:1.00 (for the first quarter of 2025), (iv) 5.00:1.00 (for the second quarter of 2025) and (v) 4.75:1.00 (for the third quarter of 2025).' + 'As of the date of this report, we were in compliance with all aforementioned covenants.' (10-K Item 7 / Note Long-Term Debt)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the Feb 12, 2024 amendment exists in EDGAR 8-K stream and matches the step-down schedule disclosed; Mode B — derive: covenant amended within ~3 weeks of merger close (Jan 25, 2024) and stepped back to 4.75x over 6 quarters implies management already knew pro-forma leverage would breach the unamended 4.50x covenant immediately upon closing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 8-K dated 2024-02-15 (accession 0001628280-24-004991) confirms Amendment No. 2 execution date 2024-02-12 — 18 days after deal close. Pro-forma combined debt at close: $725M senior secured notes + $1,125M new term loans + $400M assumed revolver + $1,200M assumed Omni first-lien + $80M assumed Omni revolver + $245M assumed Omni second-lien ~= $3.775B gross debt against a sub-$200M trailing EBITDA from the Forward Air standalone (op-income FY23 from continuing operations: ~$84M after $53M 'other operations' loss; legacy Expedited+Intermodal contribution ~$140M). The 4.50x->6.00x step-up gives ~33% covenant headroom on a leverage metric that is already structurally near the looser cap.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Pre-emptive covenant relief 18 days post-close, with a 6-quarter step-down that does not return to the original 4.50x until late 2025, is a textbook distressed-credit signal. The 'in compliance' framing is technically true but conceals that compliance exists ONLY because the lender granted relief BEFORE the first measurement date. Top forensic signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On October 31, 2023, Omni filed a complaint (the Omni Complaint) against us and certain of its direct and indirect subsidiaries in the Court of Chancery in the State of Delaware. The Omni Complaint alleged, among other things, that we breached our obligation to close the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement and sought specific performance to compel us to close and related declaratory relief. On January 22, 2024, we, Omni, and certain other parties to the Merger Agreement entered into Amendment No. 1 ... the parties to the Amended Merger Agreement completed the Omni Acquisition. The case remains pending.' (10-K Legal Proceedings / Subsequent Events)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify litigation timeline against Delaware Chancery docket via 8-K stream; Mode B — derive: management attempted to walk from the deal, was sued for specific performance, and closed under amended (presumably less-favorable-to-FWRD) terms — what changed in the Amended Merger Agreement?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Subsequent Events + 8-K stream Aug 2023 - Jan 2024 (16+ 8-Ks filed during this window per edgar.list_filings)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 8-K density Sep-Jan 2024 = ~14 filings vs ~3 in same window prior year. ClearBridge Investments publicly opposed the merger Aug 18, 2023 (cited in 10-K risk factors). Original Merger Agreement dated Aug 10, 2023; Amendment No. 1 dated Jan 22, 2024 reduced the cash/stock mix and altered Omni Holders' equity stake. The fact that the company tried to terminate the deal then closed it under litigation pressure means closing was NOT management's first-choice outcome at closing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Closing a transaction that you (the buyer) attempted to walk away from, under threat of specific performance, while shareholder activist (ClearBridge) is publicly opposed, is the structural definition of a forced bad acquisition. The 10-K language treats this as procedural ('the case remains pending') and buries the substance. Mode-B implication: post-close governance and integration will be hostile, and the activist will return.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Following the Omni Acquisition, the market price of our common stock decreased substantially and is currently trading at significantly lower levels than prior to the announcement of the Omni Acquisition.' + Signature block: '/s/ Michael L. Hance — Interim Chief Executive Officer, Chief Legal Officer and Secretary — March 15, 2024 (Principal Executive Officer)'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify identity of signing CEO via 8-K Item 5.02 (officer changes) and EDGAR Form 4 reporting-owner stream; Mode B — derive: a public-company CEO transition concurrent with closing a $3.8B leveraged acquisition is a leadership-vacuum signal — who left, when, why?
rfm_tuples.M_source: edgar.list_filings(0000912728) — 8-Ks Jan-Mar 2024; 10-K signature block + executive officer table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Filing is signed by Chief Legal Officer acting as INTERIM CEO and Principal Executive Officer. Prior CEO Thomas Schmitt (employment agreement dated 2018) is referenced in exhibits 10.22/10.23 but is no longer listed in current officer table. 8-K stream contains multiple Item 5.02 filings late 2023 / early 2024 (e.g., 0001628280-24-007719 dated 2024-02-29; 0000950157-24-000074 dated 2024-01-24). The 10-K is signed by the CLO doubling as interim CEO with no permanent successor named.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Closing the largest acquisition in company history with an interim CEO who is also the Chief Legal Officer (i.e., the company's lawyer doubling as its operator) is a severe governance signal. There is no permanent CEO to integrate Omni, hit the deleveraging targets, and defend against the activist. The CEO who initiated the deal (Schmitt) is no longer signing the 10-K. Mode-B finding: this leadership vacuum is the highest-stakes single risk in the filing and is NOT flagged in the risk-factors section.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In 2023, Expedited Freight's ten largest customers accounted for approximately 33% of its revenue and no single customer had revenue greater than 10% of Expedited Freight revenue for 2023.' + 'In 2023, Intermodal's ten largest customers accounted for approximately 28% of its operating revenue and had no single customer with revenue greater than 10% of Intermodal revenue for 2023.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify customer concentration disclosure consistency vs prior 10-K; Mode B — derive: Omni is an asset-light freight forwarder serving 'integrated air cargo carriers' — does adding Omni concentrate exposure to a small number of forwarders/airlines that were ALREADY among Expedited's 'ten largest'? The filing does not say.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Business Section (Expedited Freight customers, Intermodal customers)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disclosed top-10 concentration is moderate (33% / 28%) and no >10% single customer. However, the filing provides NO pro-forma combined customer concentration after Omni and gives no overlap analysis between Forward Air's existing top-10 forwarders/airlines and Omni's own forwarder customer base. Omni's business is explicitly described as 'asset-light, high-touch logistics' — the same customer pool. Counterparty mirror via edgar_fts on 'Forward Air' in 10-K filings of large forwarders/airlines is required to test customer overlap and was not run by management.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Standalone concentration is benign but the merged-entity concentration is not disclosed. Mode-B finding: high probability of customer concentration WORSENING post-close because Omni's customer base overlaps with Forward's Expedited segment, and the company chose not to provide pro-forma concentration. Flag for active monitoring; not scorable as a hard short signal absent the counterparty mirror data.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In connection with the Omni Acquisition, we, Opco, Omni Holders and certain other parties entered into a tax receivable agreement (the Tax Receivable Agreement), which sets forth the agreement among the parties regarding the sharing of certain tax benefits realized by us ...' + 'Up-C structure places significant limitations on our cash flow because our principal asset is our interest in Opco' (Risk Factors)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify Up-C / TRA structure references match (i) 10-K Note on Tax Receivable Agreement, (ii) Risk Factors, (iii) Omni Holders' SC 13D filing; Mode B — derive cash leakage: TRA payments to Omni Holders flow ahead of common-stockholder distributions and survive even if Omni's anticipated synergies do NOT materialize.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Tax Receivable Agreement section + SC 13D filed 2024-02-05 (REP Omni Holdings 4.2% beneficial owner) + Up-C structure description
rfm_tuples.M_value: Up-C structure with TRA confirmed in both 10-K and SC 13D (REP Omni Holdings reports shared voting on 1,152,846 shares plus 1,167,256 Opco Class B / Series B Preferred conversion rights). TRA traditionally captures 85% of realized tax benefits and pays them to legacy holders (here: Omni Holders). For a sub-$200M EBITDA company carrying ~$3.8B debt, TRA payments compete directly with debt service. The filing does NOT quantify the maximum TRA liability or provide a sensitivity table.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Up-C + TRA structures are common but in a distressed-credit context they convert sellers (Omni Holders) into a structurally senior cash-flow claimant relative to common holders. The filing acknowledges the limitation in risk factors but quantification is absent. Mode-B finding: common stockholders are sandwiched between $3.8B of debt and uncapped TRA payments to insiders.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We have concluded, as of December 31, 2023, that our internal control over financial reporting was effective ... /s/ Ernst Young LLP, Atlanta, GA, March 15, 2024' (Item 9A / Auditor Report)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify auditor identity and ICFR opinion vs prior years; Mode B — derive: auditor opinion is on the PRE-OMNI standalone Forward Air entity (Dec 31, 2023 close date is 25 days BEFORE deal close); the combined-entity ICFR has not been tested. Risk factors disclose 'in the past, Omni identified significant deficiencies in the adequacy of its internal controls.'
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Auditor Report (EY LLP) + Risk Factors (Omni's prior control deficiencies)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor: Ernst Young LLP (Big 4) — clean ICFR opinion as of 12/31/2023. Audit covers Forward Air STANDALONE; deal closed 1/25/2024 so the ~$3B Omni balance sheet is NOT in the auditor scope. Risk factor language explicitly admits Omni had 'significant deficiencies in the adequacy of its internal controls' historically as a private company. No transition / integration scope statement from EY for FY2024.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor is appropriate (Big 4) and opinion is clean — but the opinion is on a balance sheet that has tripled in size 25 days after the audit period close, with a counterparty that self-disclosed prior control deficiencies. Mode-B finding: probability of a material weakness or audit qualification at FY2024 ICFR audit is elevated. Not actionable yet but a known forensic risk.

rfm_tuples.R: Implicit claim from Risk Factors / MD&A — 'our ability to achieve the expected strategic, financial and other benefits of the Omni Acquisition, including the realization of expected synergies and the achievement of deleveraging targets, within the expected time-frames or at all' + Repeated forward-looking language re: 'cost and revenue synergies' and 'deleveraging targets'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify whether deleveraging target levels and timelines are quantified anywhere in the 10-K; Mode B — derive: a credit-led capital structure with covenant step-down to 4.75x by Q3 2025 requires roughly $750M+ of EBITDA growth or $1B+ debt paydown in 18 months — is this disclosed as feasible?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A + Risk Factors (multiple sections), Item 7 Liquidity
rfm_tuples.M_value: Filing references 'deleveraging targets' 6+ times but provides NO numeric target, NO timeline, NO synergy quantification ($ or %), and NO bridge from current pro-forma leverage to the 4.75x Q3 2025 covenant. Standalone Forward operating income from continuing operations FY23: $84M (Expedited $169M - Intermodal $32M + Other -$53M - corporate -$64M; approximate from segment math). Reach to Omni-pro-forma EBITDA capable of servicing $3.8B debt at the 4.75x covenant in 18 months is not bridged.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Repeatedly invoking 'synergies' and 'deleveraging targets' as forward-looking aspirations without ANY numeric anchor in the 10-K, while the covenant schedule mathematically requires fast deleveraging, is exactly the lying-by-omission pattern the framework is built to flag. Top-2 Mode-B finding.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the quarter ended December 31, 2023, no director or officer of the Company adopted or terminated a Rule 10b5-1 trading agreement.' (Item 9B)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify against EDGAR Form 4 reporting-owner stream Jan-May 2024 for insider transactions; Mode B — derive: under massive deal-related stock decline, what does insider behavior look like?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Form 4 filing density Jan-May 2024: 17 Form 4s filed (vs ~4-6 in a typical 4.5-month window). Cluster of 11 Form 4s on 2024-03-29 / 2024-04-01 corresponds to merger-related Up-C equity issuance to Omni Holders (per SC 13D structure). Two named-officer Form 4s on 2024-01-16 (5 separate filings same day) and another on 2024-02-27 (filer 0000950170-24-021526) reflect either pre-merger vesting/grants or post-merger initial-statement filings. No 10b5-1 plan adoption disclosed. No insider OPEN-MARKET PURCHASES detected — would be the expected signal if management believed the post-deal stock decline was disconnected from fundamentals.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Absence of insider buying after a substantial post-deal stock decline is a soft signal that management does not view the price as attractive at the new levels. Heavy Form 4 traffic is mostly mechanical (deal-related equity issuance) rather than open-market accumulation. Confirming-pattern signal, not standalone.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On December 20, 2023, the Company completed the sale of its Final Mile business ... gain on sale of $155,829.' + 'Net income decreased $25,840, or 13.4%, to $167,351 for the year ended December 31, 2023 compared to $193,191 for the same period in 2022.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the Final Mile divestiture gain magnitude and timing vs 8-K disclosure; Mode B — derive: ex the $155.8M one-time gain, what does continuing-operations net income look like, and does the headline 'net income $167.4M' obscure underlying deterioration?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Consolidated Statements of Operations + Note on Discontinued Operations
rfm_tuples.M_value: Net income from CONTINUING operations FY23: $42,803K vs $179,414K in FY22 (-76.1%). Total net income $167,351 is 74% composed of $124,548K Discontinued Operations income (which itself is largely the $155.8M Final Mile gain net of tax). Headline figure of $167.4M only modestly down YoY hides a 76% collapse in CONTINUING-OPERATIONS earnings. Operating loss in 'Other operations' grew from -$1,866K (FY22) to -$53,157K (FY23) — almost entirely deal transaction costs.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: MD&A leads with the headline net income figure ('decreased 13.4%') without breaking out the divestiture-gain effect prominently. Continuing operations down 76% YoY is the more honest read of the underlying business going into the Omni close. Combined with the covenant amendment (C1), the business is being acquired into a leveraged structure exactly as its standalone earnings power is shrinking.

rfm_tuples.R: Claim evolution between Q3 2023 10-Q (filed 2023-11-09) and FY23 10-K (filed 2024-03-15): Q3 10-Q treats the merger as PENDING with termination optionality ('either Forward Air or Omni may terminate the Merger Agreement under certain circumstances, including ... if the Merger is not completed by February 10, 2024'); 10-K treats merger as CLOSED and treats Amendment No. 2 covenant relief as routine.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify both filings' merger-status language; Mode B — derive: between Nov 9, 2023 and Mar 15, 2024, the company went from optionality-to-walk → litigated specific-performance → closed-with-covenant-relief. The 10-K presents the outcome as continuous strategy execution.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3 10-Q language emphasizes optionality and 'business uncertainties' from a pending deal. Q3 10-Q includes only 4 covenant mentions and 0 going-concern references. 10-K, by contrast, includes 14 covenant mentions and Amendment No. 2 step-down detail, but still no going-concern language despite ~$3.8B leveraged structure. The narrative arc presented in MD&A ('we closed the strategic combination') elides the Oct 31, 2023 Omni complaint, the failed termination attempt, the activist letter, and the ~3-week-post-close covenant relief.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K narrative reconstructs an embattled, contested, litigated deal closure as a smooth strategic execution. The factual chronology — buyer tries to walk, gets sued, settles, closes under amended terms, gets covenant relief 18 days later — is the most distressed-credit story arc in the filing. Strong confirming signal across C1+C2+C3+C7.

supplemental_signals.covenant_schedule: First-lien net leverage covenant: 6.00x (Q2-Q3 2024), 5.50x (Q4 2024), 5.25x (Q1 2025), 5.00x (Q2 2025), 4.75x (Q3 2025), reverting to original 4.50x thereafter

summary: Forward Air closed a $3.8B leveraged acquisition of Omni Logistics on Jan 25, 2024 — a deal the company tried to walk from in Sep-Oct 2023, was sued for specific performance over, settled in Jan 2024 under an Amended Merger Agreement, and required covenant relief on within 18 days of close (Amendment No. 2 dated Feb 12, 2024, stepping the leverage covenant from 4.50x to 6.00x with a 6-quarter step-down). The 10-K is signed by an Interim CEO (the Chief Legal Officer) with no permanent successor named, and continuing-operations earnings collapsed 76% YoY ($179M -> $43M). The filing repeatedly invokes 'deleveraging targets' and 'synergies' without quantifying either, despite a covenant schedule that mathematically requires fast deleveraging. No going-concern language. The forensic pattern is a textbook forced-distressed-acquisition with management framing the litigated close as smooth strategic execution. SHORT-tier.
